Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Right knee overuse pain with clicking, onset ~2 weeks ago, worsens after ~20 minutes of running (approx. 2.5–3 miles). One episode of mild swelling after first run, resolved with ice. No current swelling, redness, warmth, locking, or instability; full flexion/extension; no pain with stairs or normal walking. Single episode of right toe tingling after a run; no persistent neurovascular symptoms.
- Most consistent with overuse injury:
  - Iliotibial band friction syndrome (ITBFS): Supported by lateral-predominant localization (“toward the right side”), onset with increased running volume, pain starting after several miles, clicking with flexion/extension; no locking/instability. DDx likelihood: High.
  - Patellofemoral pain syndrome: Possible given activity-related anterior knee pain patterns and clicking; less supported as she denies stair pain and localization not clearly anterior. DDx likelihood: Moderate.
  - Meniscal pathology: Less likely due to lack of locking, joint line tenderness, or acute twisting injury; clicking and transient swelling could fit. DDx likelihood: Low–Moderate.
- Serious causes considered and unlikely per history and DDx: septic arthritis, inflammatory arthritis, DVT, vascular etiologies, tumor (no red flags).
- Plan per transcript:
  - Continue ice therapy.
  - Reduce running; avoid running through pain.
  - Prescribed a stronger NSAID (name not documented); do not take with ibuprofen; take with food.
  - Referral to physiotherapy for detailed assessment and initial management; in-person exam recommended.
  - Imaging may be considered after physio assessment if symptoms persist or exam indicates intra-articular pathology.
  - Safety-net advice: seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.

Management Plan
- Ice therapy and activity modification as above.
- Stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed; avoid concurrent ibuprofen; take with food.
- Physiotherapy referral sent; in-person clinical exam recommended.
- Consider imaging after physiotherapy assessment if indicated.
- Return/urgent care instructions given for red flags (persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, feeling unwell, or locking).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Iliotibial band friction syndrome (High): Lateral-predominant pain starting after several miles with increased running volume; clicking with repetitive flexion/extension; no locking/instability.
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome (Moderate): Overuse with knee flexion/extension and running; clicking/crepitus; less typical due to lack of stair pain and non-anterior localization.
- Meniscal pathology (Low–Moderate): Clicking and transient swelling possible; less likely without locking or twisting injury.
